Ollama, LM Studio or any other server that speaks the OpenAI API, on your computer or in your network. Your cards go only to that server. Choose a model it has; a key is only needed if your server asks for one. Local models can need minutes for a deck.
Ends in /v1, for example http://192.168.2.5:11434/v1 (Ollama) or :1234/v1 (LM Studio).
Most servers on your own network have no encryption. Anyone on that network could read what is sent to them, including the key.

Cost warning: asking for a deck sends your whole card list, about 22,000 tokens for a large collection, and one request can send it several times. If the answer is not a valid deck, it is sent back for correction (up to 3 tries). If a model fails or gives no deck, the next model or service on your list is asked as well. A paid service charges for every one of these. List only a few models, prefer free or cheap ones, and set a spending limit with your provider. Free models have low limits and are often busy.
One request can send your card list (about 22,000 tokens for a large collection) up to 3 times, and again for each further model if one fails. Paid services charge for every time.
Models that take tools and a long prompt. Tap to choose; the models are tried in the order you choose them. Free models are often busy, so choose two or three.
The Claude models your key can use, newest first. Tap one to choose it; tap it again to go back to the default.

Auto-scroll uses Android's Accessibility service for one purpose only: to swipe the card list in Pokémon TCG Pocket while PocketDeck scans your collection.

It does not read anything on the screen, it does not collect or send any data, and it only acts while a scan is running. You can switch it off at any time in the system's Accessibility settings.

Automating input in a game may go against that game's terms of service. You use this feature at your own risk. If you would rather not, decline and scroll the list yourself.

In the game open My Cards and choose the view with 3 cards per row. Tap Start in PocketDeck, then scroll through your cards. Optionally auto-scroll does the swiping for you; it stays off until you agree to it.
Your collection, decks and settings stay on this phone.
Tournament lists and card images are downloaded from Limitless TCG, TCGdex and GitHub, which can see your IP address.
If you add an AI key, your card list and the tournament decks are sent to that service. OpenRouter\'s free models may log them.
